sla_name: Concepts of sports, games, play, physical activity and exercise
sla_assessment_criteria: Concepts of sports, games, play, physical activity and exercise, their importance to health and well-being, and their relationship with other disciplines are clearly explained.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Sport, games, play, physical activity and exercise are related concepts of movement that contribute to health and well-being.
sla_notes_details: Play is spontaneous, voluntary and enjoyable activity done for fun. Games are structured forms of play with rules, and may be competitive or recreational. Sport is organised, rule-governed physical competition requiring skill and physical effort, such as football or athletics. Physical activity is any bodily movement produced by muscles that uses energy, including walking and farm work. Exercise is planned, structured and repetitive physical activity done to improve or maintain fitness. Their importance includes improved heart and lung function, stronger muscles and bones, weight control, reduced stress, better social skills and discipline. Sports relate to other disciplines: biology (anatomy and physiology), physics (movement and force), mathematics (scoring and statistics), geography and history (venues and origins), and business (sports management and marketing).
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, children kicking a ball in the yard are at play; a school netball match with referees is a sport; jogging for thirty minutes to improve stamina is exercise.
sla_notes_daily_life: Walking to school, farm work, playing games during break and joining clubs are everyday ways of keeping active and healthy.
sla_exercise: Differentiate sport from play.::Sport is organised, rule-governed competition, while play is spontaneous and done for fun.||Define exercise.::Planned, structured and repeated physical activity done to improve or maintain fitness.||Name two benefits of physical activity to health.::Stronger muscles and bones, better heart and lung function (or reduced stress).

sla_notes_intro: Sports can be grouped according to how they are played, the equipment used, and the number of participants.
sla_notes_details: Common categories are individual sports (athletics, swimming, gymnastics), team sports (football, netball, volleyball, basketball), combat or contact sports (boxing, judo, karate, wrestling), racket sports (tennis, badminton, table tennis), water sports (swimming, diving, rowing), track and field events, indoor sports (table tennis, chess, darts), outdoor and adventure sports (hiking, cycling), and sports for persons with disabilities such as the Paralympics. Sports may also be classified as amateur or professional, and as traditional such as bao, or modern. Each category has particular skills, rules and equipment.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, netball and volleyball are team sports with a set number of players, while the 100 m sprint is an individual track event.
sla_notes_daily_life: Pupils choose sports for school clubs and community leagues according to interest, facilities and ability.
sla_exercise: Give two examples of racket sports.::Tennis and badminton.||Name two team sports.::Football and netball.||To which category does boxing belong?::Combat (contact) sports.

sla_name: Basic tenets of safety in sports

sla_teaching_aids: Sport documentary videos Video clips safety content

sla_notes_intro: Safety in sports means practices that protect participants from injury and harm, and it includes first aid for injured athletes.
sla_notes_details: Safety is important to prevent injury, save lives, build confidence and allow continuous participation. Practices include warming up, checking the field and equipment, wearing suitable clothes, shoes and protective gear (shin pads, mouth guards, helmets), following rules, having a qualified coach or referee, drinking water, avoiding play in extreme heat or storms, and keeping a first aid kit. Common injuries are sprains, strains, cramps, fractures, bruises, cuts and dislocations. First aid follows the principle RICE: Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation. An injured athlete is attended by stopping play, assessing the injury, giving first aid, calling for medical help and not moving a person with a suspected spinal injury.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, for a sprained ankle the athlete stops playing, rests, applies ice wrapped in a cloth, uses a bandage for compression and raises the leg above the heart level.
sla_notes_daily_life: Safe behaviour on the field, such as wearing proper shoes and warming up, prevents injuries during physical education, sports days and community matches.
sla_exercise: What does RICE stand for in first aid?::Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation.||State two safety measures before playing a game.::Warming up and checking the field and equipment.||Name two common sports injuries.::Sprains and muscle cramps (or strains, fractures).

sla_teaching_aids: Pictures|Videos with the physical|Mental fitness content
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Physical fitness is the ability of the body to perform daily and sports tasks without undue fatigue, while mental fitness is a healthy, focused and resilient state of mind.
sla_notes_details: Physical fitness has health-related components: cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition; and skill-related components: speed, agility, balance, coordination, power and reaction time. Mental fitness includes concentration, confidence, motivation, emotional control, discipline and resilience. Importance: better performance, prevention of disease and injury, stress relief, teamwork and positive attitudes. Attributes of fit persons include stamina, alertness, good posture and quick recovery. Fitness is developed through regular training, balanced diet, adequate rest and positive thinking.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, running 2.4 km in progressively shorter times improves cardiovascular endurance, while visualising a goal before a match improves mental focus.
sla_notes_daily_life: Fit people manage farm work, study, and household duties with less tiredness and are less stressed in exams.
sla_exercise: Name two health-related components of physical fitness.::Cardiovascular endurance and flexibility (or muscular strength).||Give one attribute of mental fitness.::Concentration (or confidence, discipline).||Which exercise improves flexibility?::Stretching exercises.

sla_assessment_criteria: Warm-up and cool-down exercises are clearly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A warm-up prepares the body for vigorous activity, while a cool-down helps the body return to its resting state after activity.
sla_notes_details: Warm-up has three parts: general activities such as jogging that raise body temperature and heart rate; dynamic stretching of major muscle groups (arm circles, leg swings, high knees); and sport-specific drills. It takes about 10-15 minutes. Benefits: prevents injury, increases blood flow and muscle flexibility, improves performance and prepares the mind. Cool-down consists of slow jogging or walking followed by static stretching held for 15-30 seconds, and takes about 5-10 minutes. Benefits: gradually lowers heart rate, removes lactic acid, reduces muscle soreness and improves flexibility.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, before a football match players jog around the field, do leg swings and short passing drills; after the match they walk and stretch the hamstrings and calves.
sla_notes_daily_life: Even simple stretching before farm work or sport prevents muscle strains and stiffness.
sla_exercise: State two benefits of a warm-up.::Prevents injury and raises body temperature/heart rate.||Give one example of a static stretch used in a cool-down.::Hamstring stretch (or calf stretch).||How long should a cool-down last?::About 5 to 10 minutes.

learning_activity_name: Carry out warm up and cool down exercises
sla_name: Carrying out warm-up and cool-down exercises
sla_assessment_criteria: Warm up and cool down exercises are correctly carried out.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Learners perform the correct sequence of warm-up and cool-down exercises safely and with proper technique.
sla_notes_details: A practical warm-up sequence: 5 minutes of easy jogging, followed by dynamic stretches such as arm swings, trunk rotations, lunges, high knees, butt kicks and side steps, then short sprints or sport-specific drills. Perform each movement under control, gradually increasing range and speed. For a cool-down: slow the pace to a walk, breathe deeply, and do static stretches for the calves, hamstrings, quadriceps, shoulders, arms and back, holding each for 15-30 seconds without bouncing. Students take turns to lead a group and correct one another's technique.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, a class forms lines, jogs across the field, does ten walking lunges, ten trunk rotations and five short sprints as its warm-up, and finishes with a seated hamstring stretch.
sla_notes_daily_life: Learners can do a short warm-up and cool-down independently before and after any exercise session or community game.
sla_exercise: Why should stretches not be done with bouncing?::Bouncing can cause muscle tears; smooth held stretches are safer.||Give two dynamic warm-up exercises.::High knees and arm circles (or lunges, trunk rotations).||What is done immediately after a match before static stretching?::Slow jogging or walking to lower the heart rate.

sla_notes_intro: Football and track events each require specific skills, safe practice and rules of play.
sla_notes_details: Football: skills are passing, dribbling, shooting, receiving or trapping, heading, tackling and goalkeeping. Rules include eleven players per team, two halves of 45 minutes, offside, fouls, free kicks, penalties, throw-ins, corner and goal kicks, and yellow and red cards. Safety includes wearing shin pads and boots, warming up and avoiding dangerous tackles. Track events include sprints (100 m, 200 m, 400 m), middle distance (800 m, 1500 m), long distance (5000 m, 10000 m), hurdles and relays. Techniques include the crouch start using starting blocks, the drive phase, the finish lunge and baton exchange in relays. Rules include staying in lane, a false start leading to disqualification and passing the baton within the zone. Safety involves checking the track and warming up.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, in a 4 x 100 m relay the baton must be passed within the 20 m exchange zone or the team is disqualified.
sla_notes_daily_life: These skills apply in school competitions such as UMISETA and community leagues, and their rules teach fairness and self-control.
sla_exercise: How many players are in a football team on the pitch?::Eleven.||Name the three sprint distances in track events.::100 m, 200 m and 400 m.||What happens if a baton is passed outside the exchange zone?::The relay team is disqualified.

sla_notes_intro: Learners apply skills, techniques, rules and safety principles while playing football and taking part in track events.
sla_notes_details: In football, students practise passing with the inside of the foot, controlling the ball with the chest, thigh and feet, dribbling with both feet, shooting with the instep and small-sided matches with a referee applying rules. In track, they practise the crouch start and acceleration, upright running technique, arm action, the finish lunge, hurdling and baton exchange. Safety principles observed are warming up, using proper footwear, suitable running surfaces and supervision. Participants show teamwork, fairness and respect for referees and opponents.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, a class plays a 5-a-side match to practise passing and shooting, and later races 60 m sprints using a crouch start.
sla_notes_daily_life: Students take part in school teams, bonanzas and sports days and continue to play football with friends after school.

sla_notes_intro: Netball, field events and either swimming or gymnastics develop coordination and strength and each is played under specific rules.
sla_notes_details: Netball: seven players per team, positions GS, GA, WA, C, WD, GD and GK; skills include the chest pass, bounce pass, shoulder pass, footwork, catching, shooting, dodging and defending; rules include no contact, obstruction, three-second rule, holding the ball for not more than three seconds and stepping. Field events: throws (shot put, discus, javelin) and jumps (long jump, high jump, triple jump); techniques include the glide or spin in throwing and the approach run, take-off, flight and landing in jumping; safety is keeping the throwing area clear and waiting for the signal. Optional swimming: strokes (freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke, butterfly), safe entry and supervision by a lifeguard. Optional gymnastics: rolls, balances, cartwheels and vaults, with mats and spotters.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, in the long jump an athlete runs up, takes off before the board without stepping over, flies and lands in the sand pit with both feet.
sla_notes_daily_life: Many girls and boys play netball and athletics for schools and clubs, and swimming is also a life-saving skill.
sla_exercise: How many players are in a netball team?::Seven.||Name three throwing events in athletics.::Shot put, discus and javelin.||State one safety rule for swimming.::Swim only under supervision of a lifeguard or trained adult.

sla_notes_intro: Learners practise and play netball, field events and the chosen optional activity while following rules and safety practices.
sla_notes_details: Netball practice includes passing in pairs and threes, shooting at the post, defending with a distance of 0.9 m, and match play with umpires. Field events practice includes standing throws, the glide technique in shot put, run-up and take-off in long and high jump and correct landing. Swimming learners practise breathing, floating, leg and arm actions and a complete stroke; gymnastics learners practise forward and backward rolls, balances and cartwheels on mats. All activities require warm-up, correct technique, teamwork and following the instructor's directions.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, a shooter in netball stands within the goal circle, balances on both feet and releases the ball in a high arc into the ring.
sla_notes_daily_life: Learners take these skills to inter-class competitions and enjoy physical activity throughout life.

sla_assessment_criteria: Basic norms and values in sports in Tanzanian context are clearly described.
sla_references: TET(2023), SPORT STUDIES SYLLABUS FOR ORDINARY SECONDARY EDUCATION, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Norms are accepted standards of behaviour, and values are the beliefs about what is good, and both guide conduct in Tanzanian sports.
sla_notes_details: Important norms are obeying rules and officials, punctuality, proper dress, respect for opponents and spectators, teamwork and sharing. Values include fair play, honesty, discipline, respect, unity, patriotism, perseverance, cooperation, tolerance and humility. In Tanzania, competitions such as UMITASHUMTA and UMISETA and national teams teach unity and patriotism, and cultural traditional sports such as bao reflect local heritage. Violations such as cheating, bribery, violence among fans and match fixing damage sports. The National Sports Council of Tanzania (BMT) and federations promote ethical conduct.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, a footballer who admits to a foul or helps an injured opponent displays fair play.
sla_notes_daily_life: Fair play in school games teaches honesty and respect that carry over to home, work and community life.
sla_exercise: Give two values promoted by sport.::Fair play and discipline.||Name one school sports competition in Tanzania.::UMISETA (or UMITASHUMTA).||State one behaviour that goes against sports ethics.::Cheating (or match fixing, violence).

sla_notes_intro: Basketball, table tennis and tennis or badminton require quick reactions, accuracy and knowledge of rules.
sla_notes_details: Basketball: five players a side; skills include dribbling, chest and bounce passes, shooting (set shot and lay-up), rebounding and defence; rules include travelling, double dribble, three-second violation, fouls, and 24-second shot clock. Table tennis: serve, forehand and backhand drives, push and spin; rules include a valid serve, games to 11 points, best of five or seven games, and alternating serves every two points. Tennis: serve, forehand, backhand, volley and lob, scoring 15-30-40-game; badminton: serve, clear, drop shot, smash and net play with games to 21 points. Safety: appropriate shoes, warm-up, checking the court and avoiding collisions.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, in basketball a player who takes more than two steps without dribbling commits a travelling violation and loses possession.
sla_notes_daily_life: These games are played in schools, gyms and clubs and develop fast thinking and coordination.
sla_exercise: How many players from one basketball team are on the court?::Five.||To how many points is a table tennis game played?::Eleven points.||Give one basketball violation.::Travelling (or double dribble).

sla_notes_details: In basketball they practise dribbling with either hand, passing in moving triangles, shooting lay-ups and playing 3-on-3 games. In table tennis, they practise the grip, serve, forehand and backhand drives and play singles matches keeping score. In tennis or badminton, they practise the grip, serve and rallying, and play games observing the boundary lines. sla_notes_illustrations: For example, a class plays small-sided 3-on-3 basketball on half court to practise passing, screening and shooting.
sla_notes_daily_life: Learners continue to play these sports during leisure time in clubs and community centres.

sla_notes_intro: Risk behaviours in sports are harmful practices such as doping and substance abuse that endanger health and violate fair play.
sla_notes_details: Doping is the use of banned substances or methods to enhance performance, such as anabolic steroids, stimulants, diuretics, blood doping and human growth hormone. Substance abuse includes misuse of alcohol, tobacco, cannabis and other drugs. Reasons include pressure to win, wish for money and fame, peer influence and lack of knowledge. Effects include heart disease, liver damage, hormonal imbalance, addiction, mental problems, bans and loss of medals, damaged reputation and death. Mitigation includes education, testing by the World Anti-Doping Agency and the national anti-doping body, strict penalties, counselling, positive role models and healthy alternatives such as good nutrition and proper training.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, an athlete who tests positive for steroids can be banned from competition and stripped of medals.
sla_notes_daily_life: Young people must avoid alcohol, cigarettes and drugs, which harm health and school performance as well as sport.
sla_exercise: Define doping.::The use of banned substances or methods to improve sports performance.||State two effects of substance abuse on an athlete.::Health damage (such as liver or heart damage) and a ban from competition.||Give one way of preventing doping.::Education and regular testing (or strict penalties).

sla_notes_intro: Volleyball, handball and the optional cricket or hockey are team sports with defined skills, rules and safety practices.
sla_notes_details: Volleyball: six players; skills include the underhand serve, overhead serve, dig, set, spike and block; rules include three touches per side, rotation, rally-point scoring to 25 points and a net violation. Handball: seven players; skills include passing, catching, dribbling, jump shot and goalkeeping; rules include three steps, three seconds, the goal area and 7 m penalty throw. Cricket: eleven players; skills are batting strokes, bowling, fielding and wicket keeping; rules include overs, LBW, no-ball and wide. Hockey: eleven players; skills are dribbling, push pass, hit, flick and tackling with the stick; rules include no raising the stick and no use of the back of the stick. Safety: protective gear (pads, helmets, shin guards, mouth guard), warm-up and a safe playing area.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, in volleyball a team may touch the ball at most three times before returning it, usually receiving, setting and spiking.
sla_notes_daily_life: These sports are played in schools and clubs and are suitable for building teamwork and strength.

sla_notes_intro: Nutrition provides the energy and nutrients for training and competition, and it influences body composition and performance.
sla_notes_details: Nutrients are carbohydrates (main energy source), proteins (build and repair muscles), fats (long-term energy), vitamins and minerals (regulate body processes) and water (prevents dehydration). Athletes need a balanced diet in the right quantity and timing: a carbohydrate-rich meal 2-3 hours before an event, fluids before, during and after, and protein and carbohydrates after training for recovery. Body composition is the proportion of fat, muscle, bone and water in the body; it is measured by BMI, skinfold callipers or waist-hip ratio. Different sports favour different compositions, for example lean bodies for marathon runners and greater muscle mass for throwers. Poor nutrition leads to fatigue, poor performance, injuries and illness, while excessive weight loss or unhealthy diets harm health.
sla_notes_illustrations: For example, a long-distance runner eats ugali, rice or bananas before a race for energy and drinks water to prevent dehydration.
sla_notes_daily_life: Choosing balanced local foods such as beans, vegetables, fruits, milk and grains supports health and physical activity for everybody.
sla_exercise: Which nutrient is the main source of energy for athletes?::Carbohydrates.||What is body composition?::The proportion of fat, muscle, bone and water in the body.||State one effect of poor nutrition on an athlete.::Fatigue and poor performance (or increased risk of injury).
